items.title: The Big Interview: Tim Lardner
items.raw_excerpt: Association for Project Management spoke with Tim Lardner, Regional Director for Europe and Central Asia at the United Nations Office for Project Services (UNOPS). He shares insights on the challenges of delivering projects in war-torn countries, highlights the critical role of monitoring and evaluation in high-risk settings, and reflects on the transformative impact of inspiring leaders on communities.

items.title: The Big Interview: James Garner
items.raw_excerpt: In this exclusive interview, James Garner, Head of AI and Data at global property and construction consultancy Gleeds, shares his insights on how artificial intelligence can support the project profession – and what practitioners need in place to use it effectively.

items.title: The Big Interview: Chris Bird MBE
items.raw_excerpt: Has business thinking kept up with the changing nature of risk? And are leaders viewing risk correctly? Chris Bird MBE, Director at Riskwell, shares his expert views on managing risk, embedding processes and how leaders can adapt their thinking. He also offers insight on how effective (and ineffective) risk management impacts business performance.

items.title: The multi-generational project team isn’t a challenge: It’s a leadership opportunity
items.raw_excerpt: Walk into almost any project or programme environment in the UK today and you will see it straight away: early‑career graduates working alongside colleagues with 30+ years’ experience. This may have been uncommon in the past but isn’t unusual anymore. It’s the norm. Soon, there’ll be no need to say “multi-generational team”, as simply “team” will suffice.

items.title: Good governance in 2026: Less about process, more about behaviour
items.raw_excerpt: Governance has always been important and after hosting a recent webinar, it reinforced something that I have been observing for some time: governance in 2026 is becoming less about structures and processes and more about the quality of decisions, behaviours and organisational culture.

items.raw_excerpt: Ein Minimum Viable PMO schafft früh Mehrwert durch klare Managementanforderungen, schlanke Services und schrittweise Weiterentwicklung im Projektalltag.

items.raw_excerpt: Projektleitung zwischen Stakeholdern steht oft vor strukturellen Konflikten. Beim PM Forum 2026 geht es um Verantwortung, Rollen und Eskalationswege.

items.raw_excerpt: Projektleitung zwischen Stakeholdern kann strukturell einsam sein. Klare Rollen und Eskalationswege schaffen Orientierung im Projektalltag.

items.title: AI ethics in project management: Who is responsible when the algorithm gets it wrong?
items.raw_excerpt: Consider the scenario: an Artificial Intelligence (AI) tool flags a supplier as high risk, and the project drops them. Later, it turns out the model was wrong. So, who was responsible for that call? The challenge we have is that in most projects right now, nobody has a good answer.
